---------------------------------------- Snippet Creation & Management ---------------------------------------- I’d like a more graceful way to write snippets. Ideally, a mechanism where I can write a script first, then enter a “convert to snippet” mode that lets me tokenize parts of it with variables and other snippet features.  I’d love a better way to deploy snippets across different team members and installs. For example, allowing VS Code to read snippets from a gist URL or a shared configuration file within the loaded repository.  ---------------------------------------- Settings & Configuration Portability ---------------------------------------- Many settings could benefit from the ability to read from an external location like a gist URL or a file in the loaded repo. I’d love to feed a gist to a new vanilla install and have it automatically do things like  * Load a common set of extensions * Create the list of server connections * Set specific keyboard shortcuts (e.g., bind F5 to execute SQL rather than debug) * Set the default language for new text files * Apply other small configuration details I typically have to manually adjust on a fresh install  ---------------------------------------- Data & Connection UX ---------------------------------------- I miss the yellow background of NULL cells from SSMS—it was a helpful visual indicator.  I miss the dataset summary and visualizations that were available in Azure Data Studio. These may exist in VS Code via an extension or setting, but they aren’t immediately visible the way they were in ADS.  Connection details are less obvious than I’d like. When checking “am I on test or prod?” I have to look for small text indicators. I’d prefer if the connection display were color-coded to match the group color defined in the connection manager.  ---------------------------------------- Git Integration & Visual Feedback ---------------------------------------- Interacting with Git repositories is less intuitive than I’d like. I can do everything in VS Code, but I often switch to SourceTree to double-check my actions. The visual cues in SourceTree better support and reinforce the user. Rebasing the local commit tree, in particular, is much more intuitive there.  ---------------------------------------- UI Customization & Accessibility ---------------------------------------- I like the command palette, but when I evangelize VS Code, many people mention missing toolbar buttons. Consider adding an optional toolbar UI that users can configure with buttons mapped to palette actions. You could even predefine a toolbar that recreates many of the SSMS buttons. This might help bridge the gap for users who are turned off by needing to dig into the command palette or menus. That said, if the goal is to move users away from toolbar-based UIs, this would undercut that effort.
